newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks close firmer, volumes improving.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks close firmer, volumes improving.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed higher on Tuesday, helped by interest in HSBC Holdings, while trading volumes appeared to be slowly increasing, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index finished up 110.73 points or 0.90 percent at 12,398.57. Turnover was HK$6.85 billion.
"Certainly as of a few days ago, I think the lion's share of the selling has been cleaned up," said Glenn Lesko, head of sales trading at HG Asia, adding that turnover was improving.
Last Friday's HK$4.91 billion turnover was the lowest for a full-day session since September 26.
"In the afternoon, some buying interest was seen -- basically just on Hongkong Bank (HSBC Holdings)," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
The interest in HSBC Holdings came from European inveestors, Ng added.
HSBC rose HK$1.50 to end the day at HK$180, continuing to regain last week's losses, when it was one of the counters that bore the brunt of a market selloff after the Easter break.
"I think it (HSBC) was just oversold in the past few days. It's just catching up," said an analyst who followed HSBC, adding that the bank was still a buy at HK$180.
